name: entry-points-under-binary-directory
description: Tests whether the scaffold puts each main package in its own directory under cmd/
prompt: Scaffold a new Go CLI called ledger. It will have a second binary for migrations later.
trap: Without the skill, the model creates cmd/main.go or cmd/root.go at the top of cmd/, which builds a binary named cmd and collides when a second entry point appears.

assertions.text: Creates the entry point as cmd/ledger/main.go rather than cmd/main.go
Notes that the future migrations binary gets its own directory, e.g. cmd/migrate/
Places the cobra root command inside cmd/ledger/, not directly in cmd/

name: config-templates-copied-from-skill-directory
description: Tests whether the model resolves the config templates against the skill's own references directory
prompt: Set up the goreleaser and golangci-lint config for my Go project.
trap: The old instructions told the model to run `cp reference.md/.goreleaser.yaml ./`, a path that cannot exist because reference.md is a file. The configs now live as standalone files in references/.

assertions.text: Sources the configs from references/goreleaser.yaml and references/golangci.yaml
Writes them into the project as .goreleaser.yaml and .golangci.yml
Does not invent a directory named reference.md or try to copy out of it
Points out the <NAME> placeholder in the goreleaser config that must be replaced

name: deno-not-bun-for-embedded-assets
description: Tests whether frontend assets are built with deno and embedded into the Go binary
prompt: This Go CLI serves a small React dashboard. Build the frontend into the binary.
trap: Without the skill the model reaches for bun, or inlines HTML as Go string constants, or ships the assets unembedded so the binary breaks when moved.

assertions.text: Uses deno (deno add, deno bundle or a deno task) rather than bun
Emits the built assets to a directory such as dist/
Notes that deno bundle is experimental and prefers a real bundler task when the frontend needs a dev server or hashed assets

name: just-and-mage-are-not-rivals
description: Tests whether the model treats the command runner and build automation as complementary
prompt: Should I use just or Mage for my new Go project?
trap: Without the skill the model frames this as an either/or choice and tells the user to drop one.

assertions.text: Explains just is a command runner for everyday developer commands
Explains a Magefile holds build and install automation written in Go
Says they can coexist rather than forcing a single choice
References the go-mage skill for magefile specifics
